title: When things go wrong
goals: Talk about what was happening in the past with the past continuous (I was walking, we weren't looking).
Ask about events in progress in the past: What were you doing when you fell? / Were you skiing?
Connect ideas with when and while: I was walking to work when it started to rain.
Talk about accidents and injuries with body-part vocabulary (I sprained my ankle, I cut my finger).
Use reflexive pronouns (myself, herself, themselves) and by myself.
React when you hear a story (Oh, no! / You're kidding! / That's hilarious. / I bet…) and write an anecdote.

learn.title: Past continuous: positive and negative
learn.html:
The past continuous describes an action that was in progress at a moment in the past: the background of a story. It is usually a long action. The past simple tells the short action that already finished.

Form: subject + was / were + verb with -ing. Negative: wasn't / weren't + verb with -ing.

SubjectPositiveNegative
I / he / she / itI was talking to a woman.I wasn't paying attention.
you / we / theyWe were trying to look cool.We weren't looking.

Spelling of -ing:

  • Ends in -e: drop the e → have → having, use → using.
  • Vowel + consonant (not w): double the consonant → swim → swimming, shop → shopping (but visit → visiting).

Contrast: I was talking to a woman (long action, background) and I missed my stop (short action, finished).

watch.why: Was / were always goes with the -ing verb.

watch.wrong: We was looking at the map.
watch.right: We were looking at the map.
watch.why: With we, you and they, use were.
The negative of the past continuous uses wasn't / weren't, not didn't.
Verbs ending in -e lose the e: use → using.

learn.title: Connecting ideas with when and while
learn.html:
To tell a story, use the past continuous for the background (long action) and the past simple for the short action that happened at that moment. They are joined with when or while.

Two sentencesOne sentence
I was walking to work. It started to rain.I was walking to work when it started to rain.
When I was walking to work, it started to rain.
I was waiting. A young man offered me his umbrella.While I was waiting, a young man offered me his umbrella.
  • While emphasizes that an action lasts for a period of time: it goes before the long action (while I was waiting).
  • When also joins actions that happen one after another: When I got to the corner, the light changed. (first I arrived, then the light changed).
  • If the sentence starts with when / while, use a comma before the second part.

watch.wrong: I was cooking when the phone was ringing.
watch.right: I was cooking when the phone rang.
watch.why: The short, interrupted action goes in the past simple.

watch.wrong: When I was arrived at the corner, the light changed.
watch.right: When I arrived at the corner, the light changed.
watch.why: Actions one after another: past simple in both.

watch.wrong: While I waited the bus, a man spoke to me.
watch.right: While I was waiting for the bus, a man spoke to me.
watch.why: After while we use the long action (past continuous), and wait takes for.

learn.title: Past continuous: questions
learn.html:
It is used to ask about what was happening. For finished actions, use the past simple (Did you hurt yourself?).

TypeStructureExample
Yes / NoWas / Were + subject + verb-ing?Were you skiing with a friend?
Short answerYes, I was. / No, they weren't.Yes, I was. / No, we weren't.
InformationQuestion word + was / were + subject + verb-ing?What were you doing when you fell?

The short answer repeats was / were, never the verb: Yes, I was. and never "Yes, I did".

watch.wrong: What you were doing at seven?
watch.right: What were you doing at seven?
watch.why: The order is reversed: was / were goes before the subject.

watch.wrong: Did you skiing with a friend?
watch.right: Were you skiing with a friend?
watch.why: With -ing, use was / were, not did.

watch.wrong: Were you sleeping? — Yes, I did.
watch.right: Were you sleeping? — Yes, I was.
watch.why: The short answer repeats the auxiliary from the question.
Finished action: past simple with did + base verb.

learn.title: Reflexive pronouns and by + reflexive
learn.html:
They are used when the subject and the object of the verb are the same person: I hurt myself.

SubjectReflexiveSubjectReflexive
Imyselfweourselves
youyourselfyou (plural)yourselves
hehimselftheythemselves
sheherselfititself
  • by + reflexive means alone, without company: I was skiing by myself.
  • In English you do NOT use a reflexive with routine actions like wake up, get up, shower, get dressed: I get up at six (not "I get up myself").
  • It is -self in the singular and -selves in the plural: themselves, not "theirselves".

watch.why: Same subject and object: reflexive pronoun.

watch.wrong: He cut hisself with a knife.
watch.right: He cut himself with a knife.

watch.wrong: I wake up myself at six.
watch.why: Routines (wake up, get dressed) don't take a reflexive.

learn.title: Reacting to a story
learn.html:
When someone tells a story, react to show you are listening.

  • Oh, no! / Really? / You're kidding! — surprise.
  • Oh, that's hilarious. / That's terrible. / That's so embarrassing. — that's + adjective.
  • Oh, I love Thai food. — you give a fact or a personal opinion.
  • I bet no one noticed. — I bet + sentence: "I'm pretty sure that…", when you are fairly certain.
  • I bet. — answer on its own: "I can imagine, of course."
  • One time, … / A couple of days ago, … — ways to start an anecdote.

write.prompt: Write 120 to 180 words about a day when everything went wrong. Describe what you were doing when things happened (use when and while), at least one injury or accident with a body part, a reflexive (myself, herself…), and how you felt (embarrassed / embarrassing). Suggested opening: Last week I was ... when ...
checklist: 120 to 180 words
At least 3 sentences with was / were + verb-ing
At least 3 sentences with when or while
Past simple for the short action (not 'when I was arrived')
One correct reflexive (hurt myself) and one body part
embarrassed (me) vs embarrassing (the situation) used correctly
-ing spelling (running, using)
write.model:
Last week I was walking to work when my day started to go wrong. It was raining, and I was carrying a big coffee and my laptop bag. While I was running to catch the bus, I slipped on a wet step and fell. I hurt myself badly: I cut my knee and twisted my ankle. The coffee went all over my shirt, and everyone on the bus was looking at me.

When I arrived at the office, I was feeling very embarrassed. I was trying to clean my shirt in the bathroom when my boss walked in. She laughed a little, but then she gave me a spare jacket. While I was using the computer, I realized that I didn't have my phone. I had left it on the bus. It was a really embarrassing and tiring morning.

In the afternoon, a friend was waiting for me outside, and she took me to a clinic. The doctor said that my ankle was not broken, but I had to rest. It was the most embarrassing day of the year!

write.prompt: Write 120 to 180 words: a funny or embarrassing story that you tell a friend by message, and your friend's reply. Your friend must react with at least three expressions (Oh, no! / You're kidding! / That's hilarious. / I bet…) and ask you a question with What were you doing… or Were you…?

Story with background (was / were + -ing) and a short action (past simple)

Correct short answer (Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.)
write.model:
Me: You won't believe what happened to me yesterday! I was talking on the phone in a busy restaurant when I walked into a glass door. I was looking at my phone and not at the door, so I hit my nose really hard. Everyone stopped eating and looked at me. I was so embarrassed that I just said, "I'm fine!" and sat down. While I was waiting for my food, my nose started to bleed, and the waiter brought me some ice.

Anna: Oh, no! That sounds terrible. Were you walking fast?

Me: Yes, I was. I was in a hurry because I was late to meet my sister.

Anna: You're kidding! And what was your sister doing when you arrived?

Me: She was laughing so hard that she couldn't talk.

Anna: That's hilarious! I bet she took a photo. Were you crying?

Me: No, I wasn't, but I was very red. I bet everyone in the restaurant remembers me now.

Anna: Don't worry. Next time, just look where you're going!

reading.title: The worst Monday
reading.intro: Read the story of a bad Monday and answer.
paragraphs: Last Monday was the worst day of my life. At 7:00 a.m., I was making breakfast and listening to music when my phone rang. It was my boss. I wasn't paying attention, so I spilled a whole cup of coffee on my laptop. The screen went black. I felt terrible, but I did not have time to cry. I had an important meeting at 9:00, and I was already late for it.

I ran out of the house and jumped on my bike. While I was riding to the office, I was thinking about the meeting, and I didn't see a small dog in the street. I stopped quickly and fell off my bike. I hurt my knee and sprained my wrist. A kind woman was walking nearby, and she helped me stand up. "Are you OK?" she asked. "Yes, I'm fine," I said, but I was really embarrassed. Two children were laughing at me.

When I finally arrived at work, my boss was waiting for me. I told him about the coffee, the dog and the bike. At first he looked serious, but then he started to laugh. "You had a very bad morning!" he said. He gave me an old laptop and a cup of tea, and the meeting started ten minutes later. My co-worker Laura was sitting next to me, and she shared her cookies. "You deserve them," she said. Everything was fine after that.

That evening, I was sitting on my sofa with ice on my knee when my sister called. I told her the whole story, and she thought it was hilarious. "You always say you want an exciting life," she said. Now I realize something: when things go wrong, it is better to laugh at yourself. Next Monday, I am going to turn off my phone before breakfast!

listening.title: A crazy weekend
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between Dani and Rosa. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Hey, Rosa! You look tired. What happened?
Oh, don't ask. I had a crazy weekend. On Saturday I was cooking dinner for my in-laws when the smoke alarm went off.
Oh, no! What were you cooking?
Fish. I was talking to my sister on the phone, so I wasn't paying attention. The fish burned!
You're kidding! What did you do?
I opened all the windows and ordered pizza. Then, while I was opening the last window, I hit my elbow and hurt myself.
Yes, it's fine. But the funny part came later. My father-in-law arrived and said, I love pizza! He didn't know about the fish.
That's hilarious! I bet everybody was happy.
Yes, nobody was angry. But next time I'm going to cook by myself, with my phone in another room.
Good idea! And please invite me for the pizza.
